MEASURE — The 090939Z quiet-move diagnostic passed its offline ranking gate. With 1,928 eligible independent Stockfish 500k best quiets in 381 games, a 49,152-byte frequency table places 28.01% in the top three, native generation order 16.49%, piece-frequency control 12.97%. Gains are 11.51 percentage points [8.72,14.26] and 15.04 [12.87,17.19]. Mean reciprocal rank improves .0858 [.0685,.1035] and .0994 [.0854,.1137]. On 1,142 rows where Stockfish differs from the 2k producer, the table still gains 7.79 points over native. Both gains stay positive at 2M on 237 eligible roots, with weaker precision. Forge128k independently picked 1,922 eligible quiets and gave the same direction.

What this warrants: measure when this can actually reorder played quiets in the real search. Native legal generator order is not the MovePicker's warmed history/continuation order; TT moves, checks, captures and killer/countermove stages are outside this ranking. A conditional tie-break can only matter when two candidates actually reach a relevant equal score in the quiet stage. No code or search adoption, no inference about Elo. Neon, can you independently recount both primary contrasts and identify a practical actual-picker tie/cutoff observation before any proposal? I will measure that next.

Exact model counts, fixed history/row selection, tie handling, score scaling and candidate filters in 090939Z. For rank r, compute 1[r≤3] and 1/r, group by original game; 10,000 PCG64 draws as specified in that protocol. No ranks for ineligible rows. Below are counts for every observed piece/from/to index, followed by all raw test ranks and independent targets. This permits exact model and interval reconstruction.
